review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Substance composition, solutions, dispersions and phase-state distinctions; separate chemical compound from physical joining and repair stray physical/mental genera.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet; CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. OpenStax Chemistry 2e and IUPAC terminology are cited as independent checks of scientific distinctions. Source definitions are not copied verbatim; Russian labels, selected restrictions and graph mappings are editorial adaptations.
review.context_policy: All new concepts and assertions use U1 with unspecified strength. Existing home contexts and relation grammar stay unchanged. A state of matter is distinct from a material in that state.

sense_decisions.scope: Select a chemically defined substance rather than a mixture. Purity here is the compositional classification, not a guarantee about every commercial specimen or a claim about cleanliness.
A chemically mixed material with uniform composition in the phase under consideration. Keep the composition classification distinct from physical state.
A chemical mixture whose constituents are not uniformly distributed. A pure substance in two physical states is not automatically a chemical mixture.
The physical action of connecting objects. It does not imply synthesis of a chemical compound or every organizational/communication sense of join.
A solution in the liquid state. Liquid is a second genus of this restricted subtype, not of all solutions.
A solution in the solid state. Do not restrict the family to metal alloys or equate every alloy with a single solid solution.
A liquid solution with water serving as solvent. This does not make the entire solution a kind of chemically pure water.
The substance assigned the solvent role in a particular solution. Broaden the dictionary liquid-only gloss to allow the reviewed solid solution meaning.
A component regarded as dissolved in a solution. The role depends on that solution; no compulsory change of physical state or chemical reaction is asserted.
A solution at the saturation condition for the specified solute, temperature and pressure. Concentrated is not imported as an equivalent synonym.
A solution below the saturation condition for the specified solute and conditions. This is distinct from unsaturated chemical bonds or color saturation.
A solution above the equilibrium composition for the specified solute and conditions. No guaranteed crystallization time or trigger is asserted.
Intersection of aqueous solution and saturation with respect to a specified solute and conditions.
Intersection of aqueous solution and the unsaturated condition for a specified solute.

Material with a dispersed portion distributed through a continuous medium. Phase-state differences need not imply multiple chemical substances, so do not force every dispersion beneath chemical mixture.
Select dispersed particles of colloidal scale in a continuous medium. Do not import every broad colloid or macromolecular-solution sense into this restricted family.
A suspension with solid particles in a liquid carrier. Exclude vehicle suspension, hanging and interruption of an activity.
A liquid dispersed in another liquid medium. Photographic emulsion is a different technical sense; a hard colloidal-size limit is not imposed.
Particles or droplets carried in a gas. The system is not the gas alone, an aerosol can or necessarily limited to colloidal particle sizes.
Gas bubbles dispersed in liquid. Restrict this family to the liquid-continuous case; solid foam and a foaming action are separate meanings.
The solid phase state, distinct from a material sample, hardness, solidity of construction and the existing narrower frozen wording.
The atom-kind versus elemental-substance senses require their own review. Do not force this record beneath the new pure-substance category merely because of a dictionary spelling match.
Everyday water records can include mixed samples and multiple states. Do not make every existing water descendant a chemically pure compound.
Frozen wording is narrower and may include a transition/result sense; do not silently rename it to all solids.
Correct smoke from gas to aerosol, while leaving inherited production percentages and other assertions for separate evidence review.
A crystal is not automatically a chemical compound or a chemically pure specimen; preserve its existing material genus.
Existing suspension is interruption of an activity, not a dispersed material.
General mixing need not produce a chemical mixture of distinct substances; do not add a universal product assertion.
An aerosol dispenser is not its dispersed contents.
Photographic emulsion is not the selected liquid/liquid dispersion.
Alloy, metal and solid solution require a dedicated review; not every alloy is a single homogeneous solution.
Saturated chemical bonding is not solution saturation.
Color saturation is not solution saturation.
Financially solvent is not a solution component.

review.limits: No experimental procedure, numerical composition, temperature, pressure, particle-size boundary or universal solubility is imported. Saturation labels refer to a specified solute and conditions; no unconditional exclusion between saturation classes is asserted. Dispersions are not forced under chemical mixture, because differences of phase state do not necessarily imply different chemical substances. Existing water, elements, alloys, frozen-state wording, material percentages and other upper-graph candidates remain for separate review. No application test suites.

exclusion_review.decision: Retain object/phenomenon and physical/mental-process exclusions. Remove their mixed-sense or wrong-genus witnesses. The property/phenomenon pair also loses the dark-grey lighting witness; other witnesses remain pending.

review.collision_decision: Move four valid action lookup forms off chemical compound 3488 to physical joining and correctly tag the Russian verb soedinit as Russian. Keep the ambiguous Russian noun on both explicitly qualified senses. No other collision is accepted.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Normalized English spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.
